typical_symptoms: numerous reddish-brown to dark brown pustules on underside and upper surface of leaves
premature drying and death of severely infected leaves
visual_characteristics: numerous tiny elongated lesions aligned parallel to leaf veins
raised pustules that may rupture to release powdery spores
dense dusting of brown or orange spore masses on leaf undersides
yellowing or chlorosis surrounding older lesions
lesion_characteristics: restricted laterally by major leaf veins
size typically ranging from 2 to 10 mm in length
color_characteristics: yellow to light green chlorotic spots in early stages
reddish-brown to dark brown as pustules mature
orange-brown when spore mass is fresh
greyish or dark brown in older, senescing lesions
texture_characteristics: powdery due to dense mass of fungal spores
rough and raised relative to healthy leaf tissue
dry and papery in advanced necrotic stages
spatial_patterns: scattered or clustered spots concentrated between leaf veins
linear streak alignment parallel to the midrib and parallel veins
more severe infection commonly observed on lower and older leaves
distinguishing_features: presence of raised, elongated pustules releasing a powdery brown or orange spore dust when touched
strict confinement of lesion width by parallel leaf veins creating a streaked appearance
